explain.say: Here is the trip day in order. Bus at nine. Museum at ten. Lunch at twelve. Bus back at two. Home at three. Knowing the plan helps you feel calm. Well done! Your challenge: ask your teacher for the plan of your next trip.

faq.q: What if I feel worried on a school trip?
faq.a: Stay close to your buddy and teacher. Bring something calming, like ear defenders or a small toy. You can say, I feel worried. A grown-up you trust can help.
asks: I am nervous about the trip

faq.q: Why do I need a buddy on a trip?
faq.a: A buddy stays with you so nobody gets lost. You look after each other.
asks: Tell me about Stay with buddy

faq.q: How can I get ready for a school trip?
faq.a: Ask for the plan of the day, look at pictures of the place, and pack your lunch, water and coat the night before.
Stand still and look for your teacher. Or ask a museum helper in a uniform: I am lost. Can you help me find my school, please?

faq.q: What if the museum is too busy?
faq.a: Ask your teacher, Can we go somewhere quieter for a minute? Many museums have quiet spaces.

facts: Many museums show real dinosaur bones that are millions of years old.
On school trips, children are often paired with a buddy so nobody gets lost.

quiz.say: On a trip, who do you stay with?
quiz.show: Who do you stay with on a trip?
quiz.why: Your buddy and teacher keep you safe in a new place.

wrong.1: Strangers are not your group. Stay with your buddy.
wrong.2: Staying alone could mean getting lost.

quiz.say: The bus comes at 9:00 and lunch is at 12:00. Which comes first?
quiz.why: Nine o'clock comes before twelve o'clock, so the bus is first.

wrong.1: Lunch is at twelve, after the bus at nine.
wrong.2: Home time is at three, the last thing.
